TREATING THE ON-DEVICE SAFETY LAYER AS NETWORK-DEPENDENT. Severity classification and the Severity 1 lot freeze fire ON-DEVICE, inside the same local transaction as the capture, fully offline, with zero network calls; a failed hold write fails the whole capture transaction. IMPLEMENTING A WORKER OVERRIDE. No gate in the app can be overridden by the worker it blocks, or by a Supervisor or Quality Manager physically present at the device. A blocked run PARKS and the worker continues other assigned runs. Clearance is Command Center action 10 only.

CLAMPING INSTEAD OF REJECTING A LOOSER-THAN-FLOOR VALUE. The tenant-configuration registry REJECTS at point of entry and states the bound; nothing is stored. It never accepts-and-logs, never clamps. BREAKING VERSION PINNING. A run pins its package at assignment and the pin is immutable for its life; in-flight runs are NEVER re-based by any publication, adoption or rollback; scheduled-not-started runs get an explicit rebase-or-keep choice; completed runs are immutable. A version can never be unpublished or deleted — the sanctioned route back is authoring a new version forward. DEC-LIB-001 (library pointer propagation) directly contradicts this and must not be silently resolved in favour of propagation.

IMPLEMENTING SCHEDULED WORK WITHOUT THE EXECUTION GATE. Eight conditions, no bypass, including governed manual ticks; a failure moves the occurrence to `blocked` with a reason class and it stays VISIBLY OVERDUE — never silently skipped and never marked done. There is no exactly-once claim: at-least-once trigger delivery, at-most-once effect per idempotency key, and a written record of every attempt. The thing that knows WHEN is never the thing that does WHAT. Fencing is enforced by the STORAGE layer, not the worker.
